title_en: Algorithmic Impact Assessment - Client Reporting and Engagement System (CRES)/ReportIn
title_fr: Évaluation d’incidence algorithmique - Système de Rapports et d’engagement des Clients (SREC)/JeMePrésente
organization_en: Canada Border Services Agency | Agence des services frontaliers du Canada
organization_fr: Canada Border Services Agency | Agence des services frontaliers du Canada

data.projectDetailsDescription:
Background

Canada’s immigration detention program is governed by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) is responsible for monitoring and enforcing conditions imposed on individuals in Canada under the IRPA and the IRPR.

The National Immigration Detention Framework (NIDF) was approved by Parliament in 2016 to create a better, fairer immigration detention system that supports the humane and dignified treatment of individuals while protecting public safety. Immigration detention is based on the principle that detention shall be used only as a measure of last resort, in limited circumstances. In certain cases, however, detention may be deemed necessary when: 
1.	an individual presents a risk to public safety (i.e. when an individual has a documented history or pattern of violent or aggressive crimes/behaviour), 
2.	the CBSA is unable to establish an individual’s legitimate identity, and/or 
3.	the behaviour of the individual threatens program integrity (i.e. such as immigration proceedings or removal). 

When detention must take place, the CBSA uses improved risk assessment processes, developed through the NIDF, to ensure that detainees are placed in the most appropriate facility at the time of detention. 

Several factors must be considered when deciding to detain an individual, including the availability and potential use of all alternatives to detention (ATDs). Over the last eight years, the CBSA has reduced the use of detention by increasing ATDs. ATDs, such as in-person reporting, Community Case Management and Supervision, and Electronic Monitoring, are used to effectively release individuals into the communities while ensuring public safety and immigration program integrity.  

The CBSA has now further expanded ATDs by developing a voluntary smartphone app named ReportIn that allows foreign nationals and permanent residents subject to immigration enforcement conditions to report to the CBSA remotely.

The app uses facial comparison and geographic data to verify the identity and location of individuals.  

The app was developed in compliance with Government of Canada standards on applications for mobile devices.  In addition, feedback from the Privacy Commissioner was included in the development of the app and a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) has been completed.  

About ReportIn/CRES
Reporting conditions are imposed by the CBSA, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) on a case-by-case basis under the IRPA. A common condition imposed is the requirement to report on a regular reporting schedule to the CBSA. The voluntary CBSA ReportIn app will allow individuals subject to reporting conditions to report to the CBSA without physically attending a CBSA office. The ReportIn app will provide a secure process for individuals to report to the CBSA without coming in person to one of our offices while also enhancing the CBSA ability monitor individuals who report remotely.

CBSA CRES/ReportIn solution consists of:
•	A voluntary public-facing smartphone app, ReportIn, where individuals submit reports using a mobile device/smartphone and facial images as a form of authenticating the individuals’ identity. The individuals’ facial biometrics and location, provided by sensors and/or the GPS in the mobile device/smartphone, are recorded when they report through the ReportIn app and is sent to the cloud-based processing and monitoring system, CRES.
•	A Cloud-based processing and monitoring backend system, CRES, allows CBSA immigration enforcement personnel to monitor, contact and assess an individual’s reporting facial images, locations, reporting frequency, and compliance history without individuals having to physically attend a CBSA office.

Using the mobile app, the individual submits photos that are then compared to a reference photo and a similarity score is generated by a facial comparison algorithm. In addition to the automated similarity scoring, CBSA trained staff will review, for every report made by an individual, the submitted photos and a determination will be made whether the submitted photos are a match to the individual. 

The individuals’ location is also collected every time they report and if the individual fails to comply with their conditions. 

ReportIn also allows for one-way CBSA direct messaging with individuals, which will make communication with the individual using the ReportIn app easier.

Other than facial biometric data, the supplemental types of personal information collected by ReportIn includes given and family name, Unique Client Identifier (UCI), personal email address, phone number, employment information (if applicable), facial photos, ad hoc report text, location, device ID, device model, device operating system version, error message, and trace information (where error happened).  

As previously stated, an individuals’ location will be collected and recorded when the following events occur: 
•	When an individual submits their report on their scheduled reporting date, the location, sent by sensors and/or the GPS in the mobile device/smartphone, is recorded when an individual reports through the ReportIn app and is sent to the cloud-based processing and monitoring system CRES. The EnStream location will also be used and connect only to the CRES backend system.  The EnStream service operates externally from and is not connected to the ReportIn app however may be used to collect location when an investigation is opened and the individual has not complied with remote reporting conditions. 

The operational benefits of the project are:
•	Improved management of the inventory of individuals the CBSA must monitor up until they are removed from Canada or the individual becomes a permanent resident of Canada, a Canadian Citizen, granted protected person status in Canada or their temporary resident status is restored. 
•	The ReportIn validation process is much more time efficient than an in-person meeting and provides greater operational flexibility in light of fluctuating volumes of clients.  As such, the ReportIn app is expected to increase monitoring capability while streamlining costs. 

The benefits to the individuals are:
•	Improved communication, transparency and allowing more individuals an alternative to in-person reporting and improving the engagement with the CBSA. 
•	Facilitating a secure process for individuals to enroll and report to the CBSA.
•	Improving support to individuals with accessibility needs where they do not need to attend a CBSA office and providing a more accessible means to report e.g. less time off work, reduced child care cost, reduced transportation cost and/or travel time etc.  

During enrollment the CBSA staff verifies the individual during an in-person or virtual meeting. 

ReportIn uses Amazon Rekognition, a facial recognition software, to perform a comparison of a photo of a known individual against a reference photo. This comparison generates a similarity score, indicating if the individual who is reporting is in fact the individual on reporting conditions.  The software comparison performed is a one-to-one comparison and, to note, is not a one to many comparison. It is also important to note that the software does not compare images against a database of publicly collected images.

All submissions will undergo 100% human oversight. This approach ensures that human judgment and discretion are applied to the results, promoting accountability and accuracy in the system's operation.

There are three levels of review. If a facial comparison match is not confirmed, the Alternatives to Detention Monitoring Centre Officer (ATD MCO), of the Alternatives to Detention Monitoring Centre (ATD MC), may contact the individual within a day or two for a follow up investigation. If the ATD MCO is still unable to confirm a facial comparison match, they will refer the case to the Alternatives to Detention Monitoring Centre Supervisor (ATD MCS). If the ATD MCS has additional questions or they are unable to confirm a facial comparison match, they will refer the case to the Regional Inland Enforcement office for investigation by an Inland Enforcement Officer (IEO). If the follow up investigation results in the IEO determining that the individual has not complied with their conditions, the individual could be detained as per the IRPA and IRPR.

The benefits to the individual and CBSA includes process optimization and workflow automation. The software provides process optimization by analyzing large images (data sets) to identify anomalies which assists in providing workflow automation. Workflow automation allows CBSA to utilize resources in other capacities due to the remote reporting option by not requiring individuals to attend the CBSA office.
data.businessDrivers3:
The client needs the system will address are:
•	Remote reporting instead of in-person reporting will save the individual time and money by not having to travel or arrange transportation or childcare, as well as save on time away from employment.
•	Allow more individuals with a remote reporting option as the voluntary app does not require a data plan, only access to Wi-Fi. 
•	Improved accuracy of verification of identity and location given the improved technology. 
•	Increased compliance from individuals as remote reporting is easier to access than in-person reporting which will increase the compliance rates.  
•	Provide eligible individuals with a secure and convenient means of reporting.
data.businessDrivers4:
The public benefits the Client Reporting and Engagement System (CRES)/ReportIn system is expected to have:
•	Improve and modernize interactions the CBSA has with individuals subject to reporting requirements.
•	Improve the CBSA monitoring of individuals on reporting conditions through improved identity verification and location services which may decrease the number of warrants issued and benefit the public by meeting our public safety mandate.
•	The CBSA will reuse information technology micro-service sub-systems across government services and departments rather than procuring new systems and technology which will provide cost savings benefits to the public.
•	Provide a remote reporting option for individuals on reporting conditions. This will decrease the number of in-person reporting individuals, which will in turn reduce the time CBSA staff meet with individuals providing additional cost savings to the public.
data.businessDrivers6:
The improvements, benefits and advantages the CBSA expect from using the CRES/ReportIn are:
•	Enhancing compliance by individuals with an easy to use voluntary app using facial biometrics comparison for identification purposes.
•	Reducing detention costs by providing access to a remote reporting ATD.
•	Enhancing CBSA relations with individuals by facilitating a secure process for individuals to enroll and report without coming in person to a CBSA office.
•	Allowing CBSA to more effectively monitor individuals who report remotely through submission of the individual’s location at the same time as the submission of the report photos. 
•	Having the ability to receive regular updates from the individual through the app on their residential address, employment, among other things, will allow the CBSA to have relevant information on the individual that can be used to contact and monitor them for any early indicators of non-compliance.
•	Allowing for, when appropriate, an accessible alternative to in-person reporting requirements, and having an enhanced verification and monitoring system.
•	Building and maintaining relationships with CBSA and individuals will ensure individuals are fully aware of their obligations and have a process for getting timely answers to any questions about the status of their case.
•	Providing CBSA the ability to track trends and patterns of individuals (e.g. individuals that may attempt to hide or falsify their identity by submitting photos obscuring their face or providing photos of another individual, attempt to hide or falsify their location, etc.).
•	Reducing non-compliance of individuals by providing a more reliable remote reporting option that can be accessed by more individuals that will allow anyone with a smartphone or mobile device with access to Wi-Fi or cellular data to use the app.
data.businessDrivers7:
The CBSA will ensure the system is confined to address individual needs by:  
•	The CRES/ReportIn will be rolled out as a tool that enables CBSA officers to more effectively manage individuals within the community as a means to support the ATD mandate. It will provide a safe and secure remote reporting option to submit 5 facial view photos and their point-in-time location information while ensuring that individuals are not constantly tracked.   
•	Individuals required to report to the CBSA will be assessed for eligibility for ReportIn by a CBSA officer. The assessment will include, but is not limited to, the individual having a smartphone or mobile device and be willing to comply with the reporting conditions. Positive eligibility will provide enhanced accessibility to remote reporting and will provide individual financial cost savings (e.g. not having to in person report, take time off work, find childcare and/or reduce transportation costs).
•	CBSA has developed step-by-step instructions, including screenshots, for the voluntary ReportIn app and how to: download the app; create an account in the app; report and submit photos in the app; and get assistance with the app.  
•	The voluntary ReportIn app is available in 16 languages, including English and French, in order to allow individuals to have greater accessibility using the app and increase compliance with reporting conditions with the app.  
•	CBSA’s ReportIn Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) and Privacy Policy provides individuals with the appropriate safeguards for their facial biometrics information which will not be used for any other purpose (including by the supplier) than stated.
•	CBSA’s contract with Amazon Web Service (AWS) includes a nondisclosure agreement providing additional safeguards for individuals’ information using remote reporting through ReportIn. AWS will not access, use or disclose personal information except as needed to provide services under contract and/or to provide notifications of personal data breaches.

data.decisionSector3:
The decision that will be automated is the facial comparison portion of the process.**

ReportIn uses Amazon Rekognition, a facial recognition software, to perform a comparison of an individual’s report photo against an individual’s reference photo (known individual) stored in CRES. This comparison generates a similarity score, between the enrollment/reference photo and an individual’s report photo, indicating a percentage similarity score of likelihood that the individual who is reporting is the individual on reporting conditions as indicated by their enrollment/reference photo. The default similarity score for a photo match is 99%.  If a score of under 99% is returned from the software, the result is failed biometrics. If a score of over 99% is returned from the software, the result is passed biometrics. There are several reasons that a result may return at less than 99% and failed biometrics, such as but not limited to, the angle of the face is less than or more than expected, the photo is blurry, the photo is that of another person, etc.

The software analyzes the facial attributes of the face, and then returns a percent similarity score for the face and the facial attributes that are detected in the image e.g. beard, eyeglasses, eyes open, landmarks of the face (e.g. position of nose, mouth).

It is important to note that the software does not compare images against a database of publicly collected images.

All submissions will undergo 100% human oversight by a CBSA employee. This approach ensures that human judgment and discretion are applied to the results, promoting accountability and accuracy in the system's operation.

After the software similarity score is returned and displayed in CRES, each case and/or report is assigned to an ATD MCO to review. The ATD MCO makes the decision on whether or not the report photo is a ‘match’ or ‘no match’. The ‘match’ or ‘no match’ decision is based on the ATD MCO’s determination of the photo match and, when a specified location to report from has been imposed, the individual’s location when they reported. There are three levels of review. All cases and reports will be assigned to an ATD MCO for review. If an individual fails a facial comparison match or location match and the ATD MCO is not able to make a final decision that there is a match, the ATD MCO will contact the individual within a day or two for a follow up investigation. If the ATD MCO still has questions they will refer it to the ATD MCS, if the ATD MCS has additional questions they will refer it to the Regional Inland Enforcement office for investigation by an Inland Enforcement Officer (IEO). If the follow up investigation results in the IEO deciding that the individual has not complied with their conditions, the individual could be detained as per the IRPA and the IRPR.

The decision that will be automated is the facial comparison portion of the process.**

The process begins with CBSA staff determining eligibility of an individual for remote reporting. When an individual is eligible, CBSA staff provide an explanation of ReportIn to the client and obtains the client consent for remote reporting. Once consent is received, CBSA staff obtain the current client information of telephone number and email address.  

During the enrollment process, the CBSA staff verifies the individual during an in-person or virtual meeting. The individual is advised to download the voluntary ReportIn app onto their smartphone or mobile device.  Once the app is downloaded, the individual is instructed to create their account using their first name, last name, email address and telephone number. For authentication purposes, the individual is asked to input their UCI as well as a Multifactor Authentication (MFA) code sent to their email address. After successfully creating their account in ReportIn, the individual is instructed to review their contact information displayed in the app which was created in CRES and transmitted to ReportIn.  If the information is correct, the client clicks yes and continues to the next step.  

The individual is instructed to take 5 facial photo views in a randomized order (looking up, looking down, looking left, looking right and looking straight ahead). The facial photos taken at this step are the individual’s enrollment photos. CBSA staff choose this facial photo, looking straight ahead, as the reference facial photo and avatar photo for the individual in CRES. This reference photo can be changed in time due to facial changes such as, but not limited to, plastic surgery, accident, etc.

Once the 5 photo views are taken for enrollment, the individual is instructed to complete their first report. The following steps are completed:  log into ReportIn with their email address and password, verify their personal information and submit their 5 facial photo views to report. Once the 5 facial photo views are submitted in ReportIn, the 5 facial photos are sent to Amazon Rekognition for facial comparison.

The software analyzes the facial attributes of the face, and then returns a percent similarity score for the face and the facial attributes that are detected in the image e.g. beard, eyeglasses, eyes open, landmarks of the face (e.g. position of nose, mouth).

data.privacyImplementation5:
Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
Remote Reporting Program

CRES/ReportIn PIA is has been completed.
The scope of this PIA is to provide an overview of the CRES/ReportIn solution that has been established for the ATD Program, and assess the privacy risks associated with the introduction of the CRES/ReportIn solution.

Specifically, the scope of this PIA includes the following:
•	An overview of the upcoming use of the CRES/ReportIn solution
•	Facial comparison is used as a biometric identifier 

This description includes the following:
•	The systems used to support the CRES/ReportIn solution;
•	CRES/ReportIn events and subsequent activities related to evaluation and assignment of an investigation event in the National Case Management System;
•	The storage, retention and accessibility of CRES/ReportIn data.

In support of efforts to expand and improve ATDs, the CBSA has developed a voluntary smartphone app called ReportIn that allows individuals subject to immigration enforcement conditions to report to the CBSA remotely. Only those individuals expressly required to report to the CBSA as a condition of their release and choose ReportIn as the means of reporting will have access to create an account.

The CBSA will be launching CRES/ReportIn in Fall 2024 on a phased-in basis to provide enough time for the orderly transition of individuals. The app will allow for a reduction in in-person reporting or detention in situations where no current appropriate ATD exists. With the app, the CBSA also has an opportunity to build a more nationally consistent ATD that will be secure and more widely available.

The CRES/ReportIn solution is made up by the following major components: Smartphone Application: Prior to initializing the sign up process, the individual must download the CBSA ReportIn mobile app from either the Apple App store or the Google Play store, based upon the individuals’ device they are using. In order to protect the individuals’ Personal Identifiable Information (PII), a Secure Remote Password (SRP) is used between the individuals’ device and the CRES AWS environment.  Amazon Cognito is used as an authentication provider that supports OAuth 2.0, Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and SRP. The mobile app utilizes AWS Amplify to interface with Amazon Cognito using SRP. Through the Cognito SRP protocol, the mobile app is utilized to implement user sign-up, user sign-in, multi factor authentication and forgot password functionality, minimizing snooping or “Man in the Middle” attack risks.

CRES Web App & Database: The main processing and storage hub for the ReportIn solution is the CRES database, used to store ReportIn individual authentication data, and the web application. The web application is used by the CBSA staff to review and manage the active cases of individuals, as well as providing ongoing as well as historical reporting capabilities. The CRES console is the main interface used by CBSA staff and provides the staff the ability to manage multiple individuals and cases in a centralized location.

Facial recognition software: To validate the individual’s biometric facial data, the app requires the individual to provide multiple biometric facial photos that are used to identify the individual for the duration of their ATD enrollment. The Amazon Rekognition software is used to perform this authentication/validation requirement. The biometric facial photos are hosted in the AWS Government in Canada (GC) Private cloud located within Canadian datacenters to meet data residence requirements.

data.projectDetailsTitle: Old Age Security Extended Absence Leave Prioritization
data.projectDetailsDescription:
Service Canada is responsible for investigating misuse or abuse of the Old Age Security (OAS) program including, but not limited to, identifying individuals who do not qualify to receive OAS while outside of Canada and stopping payment after a 6 month absence, as per the program’s policy. This also applies to individuals receiving the Guaranteed Income Supplement, which cannot be collected if they are outside Canada for more than 6 months. To assist in those responsibilities, Service Canada receives traveller information from the Canada Border Service Agency (CBSA), which is then compared against OAS claimants to identify individuals who have failed to report or have misreported their absence from Canada.

A system was designed to identify misuse or abuse of the OAS program by applying techniques of case load prioritization and optimization with the objective to focus on priority cases. The system does not render decisions regarding the recipient’s eligibility. The decision to investigate an identified individual and render any administrative decision is performed by a human investigator. The proceeding investigations will be conducted thoroughly, and individuals identified are given an opportunity to present the necessary documentation and explanation prior to the investigators producing any decisions.  

The system uses a self-organizing map and clustering model applied to data from the CBSA traveller information system, OAS pensions system, and SIN registry. This project has been conducted with oversight from the Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence in accordance with the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat guidelines.

Legal services were engaged to review the project under the terms of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making Systems which took effect on April 1, 2020.
data.businessDrivers3:
The system aims to reduce the complexity of the decisions Integrity
Operations agents are required to make by prioritizing the cases that require immediate inspection. The system will automate a triaging function by employing data analytics to identify prioritized cases. The system will categorize cases based on established program eligibility criteria by analyzing entry and exit data supplied by CBSA and ESDC program data. Without this solution, the agents will be faced with a backlog of cases that may not require immediate inspection, and further delay the processing of priority cases.
data.businessDrivers4: This system will optimize the inspection procedures by reducing processing times, streamlining the inspection/assessment process, saving costs on an otherwise time consuming process. The solution will increase the ability of the department to ensure the integrity of the program.
data.businessDrivers6: The solution will increase the ability of the department to ensure the integrity of the program. The system would be able to efficiently categorize cases based on a number of criteria including (1) length of recipient’s absence from Canada, (2) state of recipient (alive or deceased), (3) status of recipient’s OAS benefts (i.e.: active, ineligible, etc), highlighting the ones requiring inspection. The system will support agents by providing them with a list of cases that require immediate action by filtering the cases based on the set program criteria and grouping them.
data.businessDrivers7: This system will not autonomously make decisions. Instead, it will use the program criteria to categorize the cases based on priority. The Integrity Operations agent would then conduct a thorough pre-assessment before beginning an inspection.
data.businessDrivers8: The purpose of this system is to enhance the integrity of the OAS program by supporting agents in making decisions around the eligibility of clients receiving OAS (and other non-portable benefits such as GIS). To ensure that this system does not disproportionately target at-risk clients, the system will undergo an ethical review and fairness assessment.
data.businessDrivers10: This solution will enhance the integrity of the program by optimizing the process and delivering improved outcomes. The solution will increase efficiencies by lowering resource costs, reducing processing times, improving accuracy of benefits distribution by identifying ineligible recipients, and thereby improve stewardship of the program’s financial integrity.
data.decisionSector3: The system will filter the data based on the program criteria and summarize the data into groups with a grouping label and provide a summary by group.  This will help facilitate the prioritization of cases that need immediate action.
data.impact31: The system will not make any decisions autonomously. Instead, it will use the program criteria to categorize the cases based on priority. The Integrity Operations agent will then conduct a thorough pre-assessment before beginning an inspection.
data.impact20: The criteria for review are: (1) length of recipient’s absence from Canada, (2) state of recipient (alive or deceased), (3) status of recipient’s OAS benefits (i.e.: active, ineligible, etc)
data.impact21: The system will output filtered observations that are labelled and summarized by group. This will support Integrity Operations agents to identify and address the high priority cases which require verification of continued eligibility for OAS and additional supplemental benefits. An administrative decision that an OAS recipient is no longer eligible to receive benefits payments will be supported by the system’s outputs which identify the cases that are high priority and require immediate assessment. translationsOnResult.projectDetailsTitle: Priorisation des absences prolongées pour la Sécurité de la vieillesse
translationsOnResult.projectDetailsDescription:
Service Canada est responsable d’enquêter sur l’utilisation abusive ou frauduleuse du programme de la Sécurité de la vieillesse (SV), y compris, mais sans s’y limiter, l’identification des individus qui ne sont pas qualifiés pour recevoir la SV lorsqu’ils sont hors du Canada et l’arrêt du paiement après une absence de 6 mois, conformément à la politique du programme. Cela s’applique également aux individus recevant le Supplément de revenu garanti, qui ne peut être collecté s’ils sont hors du Canada pendant plus de 6 mois. Pour assister dans ces responsabilités, Service Canada reçoit des informations de voyageurs de l’Agence des services frontaliers du Canada (ASFC), qui sont ensuite comparées aux demandeurs de la SV pour identifier les individus qui n’ont pas déclaré ou ont mal déclaré leur absence du Canada.

Un système a été conçu pour identifier l’utilisation abusive ou frauduleuse du programme SV en appliquant des techniques de priorisation et d’optimisation de la charge de travail avec l’objectif de se concentrer sur les cas prioritaires. Le système ne rend pas de décisions concernant l’éligibilité du bénéficiaire. La décision d’enquêter sur un individu identifié et de rendre toute décision administrative est effectuée par un enquêteur humain. Les enquêtes qui suivent seront menées de manière approfondie, et les individus identifiés se voient offrir l’opportunité de présenter la documentation nécessaire et des explications avant que les enquêteurs ne produisent des décisions.

Le système utilise une carte auto-organisatrice et un modèle de regroupement appliqués aux données du système d’information des voyageurs de l’ASFC, du système de pensions de la SV, et du registre du NAS. Ce projet a été mené sous la supervision du Centre d’excellence en intelligence artificielle conformément aux directives du Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor du Canada.

Les services juridiques ont été engagés pour examiner le projet selon les termes de la Directive sur les systèmes de prise de décision automatisée qui est entrée en vigueur le 1er avril 2020.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers3: Le système vise à réduire la complexité des décisions que les agents des Opérations d’intégrité doivent prendre en priorisant les cas nécessitant une inspection immédiate. Le système automatisera une fonction de triage en utilisant l’analyse de données pour identifier les cas prioritaires. Il catégorisera les cas en fonction des critères d’éligibilité établis du programme en analysant les données d’entrée et de sortie fournies par l’ASFC et les données du programme d’EDSC. Sans cette solution, les agents seraient confrontés à un arriéré de cas qui pourraient ne pas nécessiter d’inspection immédiate, retardant ainsi le traitement des cas prioritaires.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers4: Ce système optimisera les procédures d’inspection en réduisant les temps de traitement, en rationalisant le processus d’inspection/évaluation, et en économisant les coûts d’un processus autrement chronophage. La solution augmentera la capacité du département à assurer l’intégrité du programme.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers6: La solution augmentera la capacité du département à garantir l’intégrité du programme. Le système pourra catégoriser efficacement les cas en fonction de plusieurs critères, notamment (1) la durée de l’absence du bénéficiaire du Canada, (2) l’état du bénéficiaire (vivant ou décédé), (3) le statut des avantages de la SV du bénéficiaire (c’est-à-dire : actif, inéligible, etc.), en mettant en évidence ceux nécessitant une inspection.  Le système soutiendra les agents en leur fournissant une liste de cas nécessitant une action immédiate en filtrant les cas en fonction des critères du programme établis et en les regroupant.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers7: Ce système ne prendra pas de décisions de manière autonome. Au lieu de cela, il utilisera les critères du programme pour catégoriser les cas en fonction de la priorité. L’agent des Opérations d’intégrité effectuera alors une pré-évaluation approfondie avant de commencer une inspection.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers8: Le but de ce système est d’améliorer l’intégrité du programme de la SV en aidant les agents à prendre des décisions concernant l’éligibilité des clients recevant la SV (et d’autres avantages non transférables tels que le SRG). Pour s’assurer que ce système ne cible pas de manière disproportionnée les clients à risque, il fera l’objet d’un examen éthique et d’une évaluation de l’équité.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers10: Cette solution renforcera l’intégrité du programme en optimisant le processus et en fournissant de meilleurs résultats. La solution augmentera l’efficacité en réduisant les coûts des ressources, en diminuant les temps de traitement, en améliorant la précision de la distribution des avantages en identifiant les bénéficiaires inéligibles, et ainsi améliorer la gestion de l’intégrité financière du programme.
translationsOnResult.decisionSector3: Le système filtrera les données en fonction des critères du programme et résumera les données en groupes avec une étiquette de regroupement et fournira un résumé par groupe. Cela aidera à faciliter la priorisation des cas nécessitant une action immédiate.
translationsOnResult.impact31: Le système ne prendra pas de décisions de manière autonome. Au lieu de cela, il utilisera les critères du programme pour catégoriser les cas en fonction de la priorité. L’agent des Opérations d’Intégrité effectuera ensuite une évaluation préliminaire approfondie avant de commencer une inspection.
translationsOnResult.impact20: Les critères de révision sont : (1) la durée de l’absence du bénéficiaire du Canada, (2) l’état du bénéficiaire (vivant ou décédé), (3) le statut des avantages de la SV du bénéficiaire (c’est-à-dire : actif, inéligible, etc).
translationsOnResult.impact21: Le système produira des observations filtrées qui sont étiquetées et résumées par groupe. Cela soutiendra les agents des Opérations d’Intégrité pour identifier et traiter les cas à haute priorité qui nécessitent une vérification de l’éligibilité continue pour la SV et des avantages supplémentaires. Une décision administrative qu’un bénéficiaire de la SV n’est plus éligible pour recevoir des paiements d’avantages sera soutenue par les sorties du système qui identifient les cas à haute priorité et nécessitant une évaluation immédiate. Avant chaque inspection, il y a une pré-évaluation manuelle par un humain pour s’assurer que les critères d’éligibilité pour l’inspection ont été rencontrés et tout le processus d’inspection est ensuite mené par un humain.
translationsOnResult.impact8: Le système ne rendra pas de décisions. Au lieu de cela, il soutient la prise de décision des agents des Opérations d’Intégrité en priorisant les cas qui seront ensuite minutieusement inspectés par les agents. Une fois qu’un agent détermine qu’un individu n’est plus éligible pour recevoir les avantages de la SV, l’individu a un recours où il peut demander une réexamination de la décision en vertu de l’article 27.1 de la Loi sur la SV.
translationsOnResult.impact10: Le système ne rend pas de décisions concernant l’éligibilité du bénéficiaire.
translationsOnResult.impact25: Bien que le système produira des observations filtrées qui sont étiquetées et résumées par groupe, la décision de procéder à une inspection et toutes les décisions connexes sont prises à la discrétion des agents des Opérations d’Intégrité. Cependant, si le système devait mal fonctionner, il y a un risque qu’il puisse représenter involontairement de manière excessive les bénéficiaires à risque.
translationsOnResult.impact12: Le système ne rend pas de décisions concernant l’éligibilité du bénéficiaire. Les cas sont minutieusement enquêtés par les agents des Opérations d’Intégrité qui déterminent l’éligibilité continue du bénéficiaire.
translationsOnResult.impact14: Le système ne rendra pas de décisions concernant l’éligibilité du bénéficiaire. Les cas à haut risque identifiés par le système seront minutieusement évalués par les agents des Opérations d’Intégrité qui déterminent l’éligibilité continue du bénéficiaire.

data.projectDetailsDescription:
The project involves building a web-based offline, on-premise application that
uses AI engines to assist with the transcription and/or translation of audio
files collected during investigations. The application will process audio files
and generate a transcription and/or translation that will then be reviewed and
edited by transcribers/translators prior to disclosure. The goal of the project
is to increase the efficiency of the transcription/translation process, not to
replace it.  It will help to reduce backlogs and improve operational necessity
by allowing investigations timelier access to relevant details of their operation
which could impact surveillance, officer safety and potential Authorization re­
writes. Transcribers/translators will still need to review the generated
transcriptions for accuracy and make any necessary edits.
data.businessDrivers3:
Transcribing and translating audio is a labour and time intensive process. The
use of AI engines to assist with the transcription/translation will reduce the
amount of labour and time required by transcribers/translators by generating
a draft transcription that they can then review and edit instead of performing
the transcription/translation themselves from scratch.
data.businessDrivers4:
Increasing the efficiency of the transcription/translation of audio files will
allow investigators timelier access to relevant details of their operation which
could impact surveillance, officer safety and potential Authorization re-writes.
It will also impact how quickly disclosure can be provided to the court,
potentially increasing the rate at which public cases are processed.
data.businessDrivers6:
The automation of the transcription/translation process will increase the
efficiency of the process by a factor of at least 10. This will allow
investigators more timely access to information important for their
operations, and enable disclosure to the courts to be completed more quickly.
data.businessDrivers7:
The application uses a login based on Active Directory to limit access to only
users with proper authorization. SOPs will be put in place to ensure the
proper use of the system.  Testing will be done, and feedback gathered, to
ensure that the efficiency and accuracy of the transcriptions/translations
generated by the application are within an acceptable range.
data.businessDrivers8:
We have considered clients' privacy and security concerns. The system is
designed by the RCMP, operated offline and on-premise. No operational data
is stored by the system. Once the transcriptions have been generated and
downloaded by the user, the original audio and the transcription are deleted
from the system.
data.businessDrivers10:
Manual transcription/translation requires a significant amount of labour and
time from transcribers/translators and has led to a backlog of audio files
waiting to be transcribed, thus delaying disclosure. This application will
automatically generate the transcriptions/translations and the transcribers/
translators will only have to review them and perform edits which is less
labour and time intensive than transcribing them from scratch.
data.businessDrivers12:
The transcription process will continue as it is now, at the same efficiency
level
data.decisionSector3:
The system does not make any decisions. Transcribers/translators will be
reviewing all transcriptions for accuracy and editing them when necessary.
The raw transcriptions generated by the AI engine will not be relied on without
that review and editing process by a human.
data.decisionSector2: The system does not make decisions
data.impact31:

data.impact20:

data.impact21:

data.impact8:
Transcriptions are never used in raw format from the application. They must
be reviewed by a human transcriber/translator for accuracy before they are
released.
data.impact10:
No impact on the rights of individuals. Audio uploaded to the system is
lawfully obtained. The application doesn't have to be used if manual
transcription is required/preferred.
data.impact25:
No impact to any individual. Voice2Text is a tool to assist transcribers at the

data.impact12:
The system does not store the audio files or transcriptions long-term. Once

user.
data.impact14: No economic impact.

data.projectDetailsRespondent: Various Stakeholders at Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)
data.projectDetailsProgram: Visitors, International students and Temporary workers and Immigrant and Refugee Selection and Integration
data.projectDetailsDescription:
AAST is a processing aid that supports staff in completing administrative tasks for immigration applications, including data-matching and bulk email creation. Two of the modules are in scope of the Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision Making. 

The modules in question, the Biometric and Medical modules, use index matching of lists of biographical information between the biometric enrolments and immgration medical examinations, and applications pending those assessments. The processing aid does not review the results of the applicant's immigration medical examinations or biometric enrollment, and only compares basic biographical data to score a level of match. This allows staff to focus on non-routine suggested matches. Once the lists are generated, the recommended information is entered into the Global Case Management System (GCMS), which is IRCC's system of record. This helps ensure that biometric enrollments and medical assessments are connected to immigration applications in a timely manner. 

AAST uses natural GCMS data points in processing. AAST does not interact with GCMS or Web browsers and it does not contain a black box algorithm. AAST does not make a decision on behalf of an employee, it makes a recommendation on matching assessments to applications. The assessments must then be entered into GCMS, and they continue to be reviewed by an immigration officer prior to a decision being rendered on the application.
data.motivation-other: Facilitate more efficient use of IRCC resources in application processing through economies of scale, assisting in managing the growing volume of applications, and allowing staff to focus on more complex tasks such as outstanding assessments.
data.businessDrivers3: The two relevant AAST functionalities allow for faster and more efficient completion of administrative tasks of recommending matches of biometric enrollments and completed medical examinations to the correct application, which ultimately reduces repeated requests to applicants and ensures smoother processing of their application.
data.businessDrivers4: With more efficient completion of administrative tasks, AAST is expected to lead to a realization of economies of scale. Additionally, since the tool can locate and recommend matches for unmatched biometric enrolments and immigration medical examinations, it reduces potential repeat requests to applicants and improves client service.
data.businessDrivers6:
• Re-allocation of resources to focus on administrative tasks that require more in depth review such as outstanding assessments. 
• Streamlining process
• Improved client service by reducing repeat requests 
• Economies of scale
data.businessDrivers7: Functionality is limited to support administrative activities with no capacity for or interface with other stages of application processing.
data.businessDrivers8: There are no trade-offs. AAST is designed to fulfill both the client interests and the program objectives.
data.businessDrivers10: The automated process allows for streamlining and review of a higher volume in a reduced amount of time, as opposed to a more time consuming and labour intensive manual approach.
data.decisionSector3:
* Medical module - By using index matching of biographical information, this functionality is able to recommend completed immigration medical examinations that can be associated to specific applications in GCMS. The functionality does not review the results of the immigration medical examination, and only compares basic applicant biographical data to score level of match for perfect and partial matches. Perfect matches can be associated with minimal review, allowing staff to focus on non-routine or partial suggested matches. AAST does not make a decision on behalf of an employee, it makes a recommendation on matching the immigration medical examinations to applications. The assessments continue to be reviewed by an immigration officer prior to a decision being rendered on the application.
*  Biometrics module - By using index matching of biographical information, this functionality is able to recommend biometric enrolments that can be associated to applications.  The functionality does not review the results of the biometric enrolment, it only compares basic applicant biographical data to score a level of match for perfect and partial matches. Perfect matches can be  associated with minimal review, allowing staff to focus on non-routine or partial suggested matches. AAST does not make a decision on behalf of an employee, it makes a recommendation on matching unassociated biometric enrolments to applications. The assessments continue to be reviewed by an immigration officer prior to a decision being rendered on the application.
data.impact31: The Medical and Biometric modules include an automated recommendation of matches between applications and unassociated biometric enrolments and immigration medical examinations. AAST uses applicant biographic details from GCMS (open applications with pending immigration medical examinations or biometric enrollments, and unassociated immigration medical examinations and biometric enrollments). It compares the biographic data points to rank unassociated immigration medical examinations and biometric enrolments with the open applications based on level of match. translationsOnResult.projectDetailsProgram: Visiteurs, étudiants étrangers et travailleurs temporaires et sélection et intégration des immigrants et des réfugiés
translationsOnResult.projectDetailsDescription:
L’OSAA est un soutien du traitement qui aide le personnel à effectuer des tâches administratives liées aux demandes d’immigration, y compris la correspondance d’éléments de données et la création de messages en bloc. Deux des modules entrent dans le cadre de la Directive sur la prise de décision automatisée du Conseil du Trésor.

Les modules pertinents, le module médicale et le module des données biométriques, utilisent la correspondance indicielle des renseignements biographiques entre les inscriptions de données biométriques, les évaluations
médicales, et les demandes en attente de ces évaluations. Ces fonctionnalités n’examinent pas les résultats des évaluations médicales ni des inscriptions de données biométriques, elles ne font que comparer des
données biographiques de base des clients pour attribuer un résultat de niveau de correspondance. Ainsi, le personnel de soutien peut se concentrer sur les correspondances non habituelles suggérées. Cela permet de garantir que les inscriptions biométriques et les évaluations médicales sont liées aux demandes d’immigration en temps opportun.

L’OSAA utilise des points de données naturellement du SMGC dans le cadre du traitement des demandes. L’OSAA n’interagit pas avec le SMGC, ni avec les navigateurs Internet, et ne comprend pas un algorithme en boîte noire. L’OSAA ne prend pas de décision à la place d’un employé; il fait une recommandation de correspondances d’évaluations liées aux demandes. Les évaluations doivent être entrées dans le SMGC et doivent continuer à être examinées par un agent avant qu’une décision soit rendue par rapport à la demande.
translationsOnResult.motivation-other:
Faciliter une utilisation plus efficace des ressources d’IRCC dans le traitement des demandes au moyen d’économies d’échelle, en aidant à gérer le nombre croissant de demandes et en permettant au personnel de se
concentrer davantage sur les tâches plus complexes, comme les évaluations en attente.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers3: Les deux fonctionnalités mentionnées précédemment permettent d’effectuer plus rapidement et efficacement les tâches administratives visant la recommandation de correspondances d’inscriptions de données biométriques et d’examens médicaux réalisés avec la bonne demande, ce qui en fin de compte réduit les demandes répétées aux clients.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers4: Si les tâches administratives sont effectuées plus efficacement et rapidement, il est attendu que l’OSAA mène à la réalisation d’économies d’échelle. De plus, étant donné que l’outil peut repérer et recommander des résultats de données biométriques et d’évaluations médicales sans correspondances, il réduit les demandes répétées et améliore le service à la clientèle.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers6:
• Réaffectation de ressources permettant de se concentrer sur les tâches administratives qui requièrent un examen plus approfondi, comme les évaluations en attente.
• Rationalisation du processus
• Amélioration des services à la clientèle par la réduction des demandes répétées
• Économies d’échelle
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers7: Les fonctionnalités sont limitées aux activités de soutien administratif et n’offrent aucune capacité vers les autres étapes du traitement des demandes ni d’interfaces vers celles-ci.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers8: Il n’y a aucun compromis. L’OSAA est conçu pour répondre aux intérêts des clients et atteindre les objectifs du programme.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers10: Le processus automatisé permet la rationalisation et l’examen d’un volume accru de demandes en un temps réduit, contrairement à une approche manuelle plus chronophage et laborieuse.
translationsOnResult.decisionSector3:
* Module médicale : en utilisant la correspondance indicielle des renseignements biographiques, cette fonctionnalité est capable de recommander les examens médicaux effectués aux fins de l’immigration qui peuvent être associés aux demandes dans le SMGC. Cette fonctionnalité n’examine pas les résultats d’examens médicaux aux fins de l’immigration, elle ne fait que comparer les données biographiques de base des clients afin
d’attribuer un résultat de niveau de correspondance pour les correspondances parfaites ou partielles. Les correspondances parfaites peuvent être associées à un examen minimal, ce qui permet au personnel de se concentrer sur les correspondances non habituelles ou partielles suggérées. L’OSAA ne prend pas de décision à la place d’un employé; il recommande de faire la correspondance entre des examens médicaux aux fins de l’immigration et des demandes. Les évaluations continuent à être examinées par un agent avant qu’une décision soit rendue pour la demande.

* Module des données biométriques : en utilisant la correspondance indicielle des renseignements biographiques, cette fonctionnalité est capable de recommander les inscriptions de données biométriques qui peuvent être associées aux demandes dans le SMGC. Cette fonctionnalité n’examine pas l’inscription des résultats biométriques, elle ne fait que comparer les données biographiques de base des clients pour attribuer un résultat de niveau de correspondance pour les correspondances parfaites et partielles. Les correspondances parfaites peuvent être associées à un examen minimal, ce qui permet au personnel de se concentrer sur les correspondances non habituelles ou partielles suggérées. L’OSAA ne prend pas de décision à la place d’un employé; il recommande de faire la correspondance entre les inscriptions de données biométriques non associées et les demandes. Les évaluations continuent à être examinées par un agent avant qu’une décision
soit rendue pour la demande.

title_fr: Évaluation de l'incidence algorithmique - le Programme d'aide au remboursement - Modèle de vérification amélioré

data.projectDetailsTitle: Repayment Assistance Plan – Enhanced Verification Model (RAP-EVM)
data.projectDetailsProgram: Canada Student Financial Assistance Program and Canada Apprentice Loan
data.projectDetailsDescription:
In November 2023, the Canada Student Financial Assistance (CSFA) Program introduced a change to the application verification system that supports the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) called the Repayment Assistance Plan - Enhanced Verification Model (RAP-EVM). 

RAP-EVM is designed to verify the information declared by borrowers, which are all factors in determining RAP eligibility and calculating RAP payment requirements, during the RAP application process (i.e. income, family size and marital status) against taxpayer information provided by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). RAP-EVM applies pre-established business rules to identify applications that meet the selection criteria. Selection criteria were determined using a risk-based sampling methodology to identify high-risk groups more likely to misreport information. The creation of risk group categories was undertaken through statistical analysis of previous cases, in collaboration with ESDC’s Integrity Services Branch. Based on this analysis, CSFA Program identified borrowers with inconsistent family size changes (e.g., if a borrower were to change their response between RAP applications to from a family size of one to a family size above one, and then revert to family size of one), borrowers who claim zero income, and borrowers who report their income just under the RAP zero payment threshold. 

Once selected for verification, a request for taxpayer information (i.e. income, marital status, number of dependants) on these applicants is made to the CRA. If the application data matches CRA taxpayer data, the application is adjudicated for an approval or refusal for RAP. If there are discrepancies, an agent with ESDC’s third-party Service Provider (SP), which operates under banner of the National Student Loans Service Centre (NSLSC), will undertake further verification directly with the borrower. The borrower will then be required to submit additional proof substantiating their information, which an agent will review before making a decision for approval or refusal of the application. 

RAP-EVM replaces the previous, non-authoritative source verification system, which required selected applicants to provide documents to prove that their reported income was accurate; RAP-EVM only requires a borrower to submit additional proof when a discrepancy is identified following the exchange with CRA.

The exchange of borrower and taxpayer information between the SP and the CRA is governed by a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) which outlines the agreement on the information to be exchanged between ESDC and the CRA as well as the conditions and procedures that will apply to the exchange of information. RAP-EVM’s data exchange process between the SP and the CRA is handled via a secure file transfer, known as the Managed Secure File Transfer. Following the exchange of data between CRA and the SP, the RAP application adjudication takes place in a closed environment. Personal information collected and used for the purposes of RAP-EVM is safeguarded under ESDC’s and the CRA’s legal authorities and related policies and directives for collecting and using personal information.    

There are two circumstances under which a borrower may wish to have their RAP decision re-evaluated. Reconsideration is for borrowers that have been refused but can show that unforeseen and unavoidable circumstances have caused them or their spouse or common-law partner to incur exceptional expenses that prevent them from fulfilling their repayment obligations. The other recourse is re-adjudication, which occurs when a borrower has been approved for RAP with a monthly Affordable Payment (AP) but indicates that their gross monthly income has significantly dropped and that they are no longer able to make their AP. 

The Program has completed a Privacy Impact Assessment which was sent to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC) in November 2023. Upon review, the OPC recommended that the CFSA Program conduct an Algorithmic Impact Assessment, as the creation of risk group categories in an automated verification process falls within the scope of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making.
data.businessDrivers3: RAP-EVM was implemented to increase the integrity of the CSFA Program RAP benefit following the Office of the Auditor General’s 2020 audit report, which recommended that ESDC take appropriate action to ensure a systemic verification of RAP applications to maximize student loans repayments. However, with the implementation of this new system, clients that are selected for verification could potentially experience faster processing times due to RAP-EVM optimizing the application verification process.
data.businessDrivers4: In 2022-2023, approximately 283,000 borrowers benefited from RAP, and of those, 90% of applicants were approved for a $0 affordable payment. Given the extent of borrowers that benefit from RAP, the introduction of RAP-EVM is anticipated to help ensure program integrity and sound stewardship of public funds. ESDC will make sure that only eligible applicants receive RAP benefits, reducing the potential for misrepresentation and misuse of taxpayer funds.
data.businessDrivers6:
RAP-EVM could result in the following outcomes:
- The new partially automated RAP-EVM system allows the program and service provider to easily identify RAP trends, which ultimately helps to inform evidence-based policy changes.
- Reduced instances of ineligible applicants receiving RAP benefits
- Reduced frequency of misrepresentation
data.businessDrivers7:
Each of the CSFA Program’s systems is governed by guidelines with respect to whom is allowed to access personal information. Specifically, each system has clearly defined user roles to control access to the database, including the use of unique user identifiers and permission settings to view, modify and delete information contained in the database.

Access to taxpayer information provided under the MOU will be controlled and limited to ESDC and SP personnel who:
• Occupy a position that requires access to this information;
• Have a valid Reliability Security Screening Clearance; and
• Have been briefed on the provisions of section 241 and section 239 of the Income Tax Act to maintain the confidentiality of taxpayer information, as well as security measures to safeguard this information as required.

Authorized personnel with Reliability Security Screening Clearance include the following positions: RAP back-office agents, managers and data analysts at the SP, CSFA Program data analysts, and CSFA Program staff working on RAP. 

Borrowers’ personal data are not allowed to be stored in the local hard drives of PCs, laptops and portable devices.
data.businessDrivers8: RAP-EVM may increase timeliness by eliminating the need for a client to provide additional documentation when selected for verification, if no discrepancies between reported information and CRA information are found.
data.businessDrivers10: RAP-EVM replaces the previous, non-authoritative source verification system, which required selected applicants to provide documents to prove that their reported income was accurate; RAP-EVM only requires a borrower to submit additional proof when a discrepancy is identified following the exchange with CRA. Automation using RAP-EVM was the preferred option to decrease the administrative burden on applicants who have no discrepancies between their reported income and proof of income provided by CRA.
data.businessDrivers12: The Office of the Auditor General (OAG) 2020 Spring Report called on ESDC to “ensure proper, systematic verification of RAP applications in order to maximize the repayment of student loan.” Failure to deploy the RAP-EVM system would limit the program’s long-term sustainability.
data.impact31: When an electronic or paper application is received at the SP, the system adjudicates the information using business rules to determine eligibility for RAP. A second set of business rules is triggered when a RAP application is approved to determine whether income, number of dependants, and marital status verification is required using the RAP-EVM. Once data submitted by the borrower has been compared to CRA data, the system then determines if proof from the borrower is required to confirm the information submitted. Throughout these processes, the system uses business rules in the decision-making processes.
data.impact20: There is a RAP formula in the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations (CSFAR), which includes family income, family size, and loan balance. The CSFA Program has developed effective methods to identify high-risk groups that are more prone to misreporting information. The program engages RAP-EVM to verify the data of these high-risk groups, as well as of individuals selected for data verification through random sampling.
data.impact21: For RAP-EVM, if the borrower income differs from that at CRA, greater than the allowable variance, a letter is generated to the borrower requesting their proof of income. The same applies to marital status and number of dependants. If the information at CRA differs, proof must be provided by the borrower. In these automated processes, there is no interpretation required.
data.impact8: Impacts from the decision are time limited since RAP approval periods last for six months at a time. During this period, an applicant can always request a re-adjudication due to changes in their income situation, in which case an agent can make changes to the initial RAP calculation decision, provided all the necessary documentation is received. In the event that an applicant receives a RAP refusal, the impact of a refusal is also most likely to be time limited, as clients whose applications are refused may re-apply when/if they meet the requirements as outlined by the CSFAR. An applicant may also appeal a decision on RAP eligibility by submitting exceptional expenses.

Given that only borrowers who satisfy the eligibility criteria, as outlined by the CSFAR, should be receiving RAP benefits, the only impact of the system is that it strengthens the integrity of the CSFA Program.

data.decisionSector3:
The following outlines the process flow of RAP-EVM:
1.	Application: The borrower submits their RAP application to the SP, indicating their previous month or current month’s income, married/common-law status and number of dependants. 
a.	On the RAP application, the borrower is informed through their consent that their data can be exchanged with the CRA.

b.	If the borrower has indicated that they are in a married or common-law relationship, then consent, name, date of birth, SIN, and income of their partner will be provided to the SP. A signed consent of the borrower and their spouse must be received prior to any data exchange between the SP and CRA. Spousal signature is a prerequisite for the adjudication of the RAP application.

c.	If the application is complete, SP calculates whether a borrower is eligible for RAP. 

2.	Selection: Those borrowers that have been identified as high risk for misrepresentation based on the risk-based sampling methods may be selected for verification using the RAP-EVM. Borrowers that are not selected for verification are assessed through the regular RAP process, including calculation (#9). RAP calculation precedes selection.

3.	Request for Information: The SP securely sends an electronic request for information to the CRA, including the name, SIN, and date of birth of the borrower and the borrower’s married/common-law partner (if applicable), to confirm previous year’s income (Line 15000 of the borrower’s tax return), marital status, and the number of dependants in the family.

4.	Response to Request: The CRA provides the aforementioned borrower's tax data to the SP.

a.	The response would occur via a secure electronic file transmission.

b.	The response would include the names, date of birth, and SIN of borrowers (and their married/common-law partner, if applicable) as well as their Line 15000 income, number of dependants and marital status. The CRA will also confirm the tax year of the data (the most recent data from the last two years requested only). If the response returns with no data, adjudication process moves to #7.

5.	Data Comparison: The SP compares Line 15000 of the borrower’s income data , as provided by the CRA to the borrower’s reported income on their RAP application. 

a.	Disparities beyond a “threshold of tolerance” in income between a borrower’s CRA tax data and the income declared on the RAP application would justify a request for additional proof from the borrower. The same would apply for inconsistencies with declarations of ‘married’ or ‘single’ and instances where borrowers report a higher number of dependants on their RAP application. The “threshold of tolerance” is determined by the CSFA Program.

b.	The SP annualizes RAP application income data before comparison with CRA borrower (and spouse/common-law partner) income data.

c.	If a family size discrepancy is identified, but the verified family income is less than the family income threshold, additional proof would not be requested since it would not make a difference for adjudication.

6.	Assessment Part One: If the borrower’s declared CRA income, family size and married/common-law status are consistent with the information reported on the RAP application, or if business rules deem no further validation required, the borrower will be assessed for RAP under the existing process.

7.	Assessment Part Two: If there is a variance between their RAP application data and their CRA tax data, or if the CRA is unable to provide the borrower's tax data, the borrower is asked to provide additional substantiating documentation.
8.	Assessment Part Three: Based on the borrower’s declared income and any supporting documentation, the SP proceeds to finalize the assessment of the borrower’s RAP application.

9.	Final Calculation and Decision: The SP runs a final calculation of eligibility, based on verified family income and size, unchanged or revised based on the requested borrower documentation. If the borrower provides additional proof documentation that differs from their RAP application data, their RAP benefit is re-calculated based on the new information.

10.	End of Process: The borrower is informed of the status of their application.

translationsOnResult.projectDetailsDescription:
En novembre 2023, le Programme canadien d'aide financière aux étudiants (PCAFE) a introduit un changement au système de vérification des demandes qui soutient le Programme d'aide au remboursement (PAR), appelé le Programme d'aide au remboursement - Modèle de vérification amélioré (PAR-MVA). 

Le PAR-MVA a pour objectif de vérifier les informations déclarées par les emprunteurs lors de leur demande au PAR, en les comparant aux renseignements sur les contribuables fournis par l’Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Ces informations, incluant le revenu, la taille de la famille et l’état civil, sont des éléments clés pour déterminer l’admissibilité au PAR ainsi que pour le calcul des paiements requis dans le cadre du PAR. Le PAR-MVA applique des règles opérationnelles préétablies pour identifier les demandes qui répondent aux critères de sélection. Les critères de sélection ont été déterminés à l'aide d'une méthodologie d'échantillonnage fondée sur le risque, afin d’identifier les groupes à risque élevé plus susceptibles de déclarer des informations inexactes. La création de catégories de groupes de risque a été entreprise au moyen d'une analyse statistique de cas précédents, en collaboration avec la Direction générale des services d'intégrité d'EDSC. Sur la base de cette analyse, le PCAFE a identifié les emprunteurs dont la taille de la famille change de façon incohérente (p. ex., si un emprunteur changeait sa réponse entre les demandes du PAR pour passer d'une famille d'une personne à une taille de famille supérieure à une personne, puis revenait à la taille de la famille d'une personne), ceux qui déclarent un revenu nul et ceux qui rapportent un revenu juste en dessous du seuil de paiement nul du PAR. 

Une fois sélectionnés pour vérification, une demande de renseignements sur les contribuables (c.-à-d. revenu, état civil, nombre de personnes à charge) est adressée à l’ARC pour ces demandeurs. Si les données de la demande correspondent aux données fiscales de l'ARC, la demande est évaluée en vue d’une approbation ou d’un refus du PAR. S'il y a des divergences, un agent du fournisseur de services (FS) tiers d'EDSC, qui exerce ses activités sous la bannière du Centre de service national de prêts aux étudiants (CSNPE), effectue une vérification plus approfondie directement auprès de l'emprunteur. Ce dernier devra alors soumettre des preuves supplémentaires à l'appui de ses informations, lesquelles seront examinées par un agent avant de rendre une décision d'approbation ou de refus de la demande. 

Le PAR-MVA remplace l'ancien système de vérification reposant sur des sources non officielles, qui exigeait que les demandeurs sélectionnés fournissent des documents à l’appui de leur revenu déclaré. Désormais, le PAR-MVA exige que l'emprunteur soumette une preuve supplémentaire seulement en cas de divergence constatée après l’échange de données avec l’ARC.

L’échange d’informations entre les emprunteurs et l’ARC via le FS est régi par un protocole d’entente (PE) qui définit l’accord sur les renseignements échangés entre EDSC et l’ARC, ainsi que les conditions et procédures applicables à cet échange. Le processus d'échange de données du PAR-MVA entre le FS et l'ARC est géré par le biais d'un transfert de fichiers sécurisé, connu sous le nom de transfert sécurisé de fichiers. À la suite de l'échange de données entre l'ARC et le FS, l’évaluation des demandes du PAR se déroule dans un environnement fermé. Les renseignements personnels recueillis et utilisés aux fins du PAR-MVA sont protégés en vertu des autorités légales d'EDSC et de l'ARC, ainsi que des politiques et directives connexes en matière de collecte et d'utilisation des renseignements personnels.    

Il y a deux circonstances dans lesquelles un emprunteur peut souhaiter faire réévaluer sa décision relative au PAR. Le réexamen s'applique à l’emprunteur dont la demande a été refusée, mais qui peut démontrer que des circonstances imprévues et inévitables lui ont occasionné, à lui et à son époux ou conjoint de fait, des dépenses extraordinaires qui les empêchent de s’acquitter de leurs obligations de remboursement. L'autre recours est la réévaluation, qui se produit lorsqu'un emprunteur a été approuvé pour le PAR avec un paiement mensuel abordable, mais indique que son revenu mensuel brut a diminué considérablement et qu’il n’arrive plus à faire ses paiements abordables. 

Le Programme a terminé une évaluation des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée qui a été envoyée au Commissariat à la protection de la vie privée du Canada en novembre 2023. Après examen, le Commissariat a recommandé que le programme PCAFE effectue une évaluation de l’incidence algorithmique, car la création de catégories de groupes de risque dans un processus de vérification automatisé relève de la portée de la Directive sur la prise de décisions automatisée.
translationsOnResult.impact21: Pour le PAR-MVA, si le revenu de l'emprunteur diffère de celui déclaré à l'ARC (au-delà de la variance autorisée), une lettre est envoyée à l'emprunteur pour lui demander une preuve de revenu. Il en va de même pour l'état civil et le nombre de personnes à charge. Si les renseignements de l'ARC diffèrent, l'emprunteur doit fournir une preuve. Dans le cadre de ces processus automatisés, aucune interprétation n’est requise.

translationsOnResult.businessDrivers7:
Chacun des systèmes du PCAFE est régi par des lignes directrices quant aux personnes autorisées à accéder aux renseignements personnels. Plus précisément, chaque système a des rôles d'utilisateur clairement définis pour contrôler l'accès à la base de données, notamment l'utilisation d'identifiants uniques et de paramètres d'autorisation permettant d’afficher, de modifier et de supprimer les informations contenues dans la base de données.

L'accès aux renseignements sur les contribuables fournis en vertu du PE sera contrôlé et limité au personnel d'EDSC et du FS qui :
• Occupe un poste nécessitant l'accès à ces informations;
• Possède une cote de sécurité de fiabilité valide;
• A été informé des dispositions des articles 241 et 239 de la Loi de l'impôt sur le revenu relatives à la confidentialité des renseignements sur les contribuables, ainsi que des mesures de sécurité requises pour protéger ces renseignements, au besoin.

Le personnel autorisé à obtenir une cote de sécurité de fiabilité comprend les postes suivants : agents administratifs du PAR, gestionnaires et analystes de données du FS, analystes de données du programme PCAFE et membres du personnel du programme PCAFE travaillant sur le PAR. 

Les données personnelles des emprunteurs ne peuvent pas être stockées sur les disques durs locaux des ordinateurs de bureau, des ordinateurs portables ou d’autres appareils portables.

Les emprunteurs peuvent présenter une demande de PAR en ligne ou en soumettant un formulaire papier. translationsOnResult.businessDrivers6:
Le PAR-MVA pourrait entraîner les résultats suivants :
- Le nouveau système PAR-MVA partiellement automatisé permet au programme et au fournisseur de services d’identifier plus facilement les tendances du PAR, ce qui contribue ultimement à éclairer les changements de politiques fondés sur des données probantes.

Étant donné que seuls les emprunteurs qui satisfont aux critères d'admissibilité, tels qu'ils sont énoncés dans le RFAFE, devraient bénéficier du PAR, le seul impact du système est qu'il renforce l'intégrité du PCAFE.
translationsOnResult.businessDrivers3: Le PAR-MVA a été mis en œuvre pour accroître l'intégrité de la prestation du PAR dans le cadre du PCAFE à la suite du rapport d'audit de 2020 du Bureau du vérificateur général, qui recommandait qu'EDSC prenne les mesures appropriées pour assurer une vérification systémique des demandes du PAR afin de maximiser les remboursements des prêts étudiants. Cependant, avec la mise en œuvre de ce nouveau système, les clients sélectionnés pour la vérification pourraient potentiellement bénéficier de délais de traitement plus rapides grâce à l'optimisation du processus de vérification des demandes par le PAR-MVA.
translationsOnResult.impact8: Les répercussions de la décision sont limitées dans le temps, car les périodes d'approbation du PAR durent six mois à la fois. Pendant cette période, un demandeur peut toujours demander une réévaluation en raison de changements dans sa situation de revenu, auquel cas un agent peut apporter des modifications à la décision initiale de calcul du PAR, à condition que toute la documentation requise soit reçue. Dans le cas où un demandeur reçoit un refus du PAR, l'impact de ce refus est également très susceptible d'être limité dans le temps, car les clients dont la demande est refusée peuvent présenter une nouvelle demande lorsqu’ils remplissent les critères établis dans le RFAFE. Un demandeur peut également demander un réexamen d'une décision sur l'admissibilité au PAR en faisant la démonstration de frais exceptionnels.
translationsOnResult.projectDetailsTitle: le Programme d'aide au remboursement - Modèle de vérification amélioré (PAR-MVA).
translationsOnResult.impact20: Une formule de calcul du PAR est définie dans le Règlement fédéral sur l’aide financière aux étudiants (RFAFE), prenant en compte le revenu familial, la taille de la famille et le solde du prêt. Le PCAFE a mis en place des méthodes efficaces pour identifier les groupes à risque élevé, plus susceptibles de déclarer des informations inexactes. Compte tenu de l'ampleur du nombre d'emprunteurs qui bénéficient du PAR, l'introduction du PAR-MVA devrait contribuer à assurer l'intégrité du programme et une saine gestion des fonds publics. EDSC veillera à ce que seuls les demandeurs admissibles reçoivent les avantages du PAR, réduisant ainsi le risque de fausses déclarations et de mauvaise utilisation des fonds des contribuables.
